A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Diffusion Bridge Implicit Models paper, with readable main text and Appendices A–H. Textual and visual comparison supports matching the methods, equations, experiments, tables, and figures without material gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original DBIM image translation and inpainting experiments, ablations, reconstruction/interpolation demonstrations, and runtime and diversity measurements in Section 6 and Appendices G–H.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including the quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–6 and runtime and diversity results in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices D–E retain the same non-Markovian bridge construction, training objective, booting-noise initialization, and sampling algorithms. The newly cited attention techniques are not incorporated into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Edges→Handbags at 64×64, DIODE-Outdoor at 256×256, and ImageNet at 256×256 with a 128×128 center inpainting mask. Reconstruction and interpolation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2–3 and 8–9, including DDBM and I2SB. The new SageAttention, SageAttention2, and SpargeAttn references do not participate in any reported comparison.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain the same metrics, training-set evaluation for translation, 10,000-image validation evaluation for ImageNet, NFE and variance-parameter settings, training budgets, and sampling schedules.

E4.justification: The variance-parameter ablations in Tables 4–5, high-order comparison in Table 6, reconstruction/interpolation demonstrations in Figure 4, failure example in Figure 5, and diversity analysis in Appendix G.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions describe timing eight batches with the first batch discarded and report runtime means and standard deviations in Table 8. Repeated-measurement information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples match throughout, including the appendices. For example, Table 3 reports DBIM ImageNet inpainting FID of 4.07 at 20 NFE and 3.88 at 100 NFE in both versions.

T1.justification: The propositions, mathematical definitions, proofs, and derivations are unchanged. In Appendix B.1, the existing sentence following Equation 20 moves from page 15 to page 16 through reflow; no proof step is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free acceleration up to 25×, the DBIM construction, its ODE and high-order solvers, and booting-noise-based encoding, reconstruction, and interpolation.

C2.justification: The explanations of stochasticity, high-order benefits, and diversity remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning low-NFE quality and dependence on the pretrained model. Appendix A's added attention-method pointer supplies related-work context without revising these interpretations or limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains the same parameterizations, training details, hardware, sampling instructions, and resource/license information. This includes eight A800 GPUs, batch size 256, 400,000 iterations, and approximately 19 days of training. The code-availability statement is unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds one sentence identifying quantized or sparse attention as another avenue for accelerating diffusion-bridge inference. Three references—SageAttention, SageAttention2, and SpargeAttn—are added; the existing novelty claims and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 revises author affiliations and contribution/internship footnotes, updates the funding acknowledgments, and adds the short related-work sentence and its references. Section organization and the scientific narrative otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Local spacing and reflow change around the author block, acknowledgments, references, and Appendix B.1, including a sentence crossing the page 15–16 boundary. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–9 retain their content and designs.

improvement.justification: v6 updates author/funding information and adds a brief pointer to attention-based acceleration in Appendix A. This modestly broadens context, but the scientific argument, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. The edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
